Gustave Flaubert, Madame Bovary, translated by Eleanor Marx-Aveling.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/gustave-flaubert/madame-bovary/eleanor-marx-aveling

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Gustave Flaubert, the author, died 1880.
- Eleanor Marx-Aveling, the translator and the annotator, died 1898.

First publication of the text used: 1886 (SE colophon: 'Madame Bovary was published in 1857 by Gustave Flaubert. It was translated from French in 1886 by Eleanor Marx-Aveling.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1886, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain. Standard Ebooks also states this in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication, and every person whose words are in the text died by 1925, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die, Eleanor Marx-Aveling, died 1898; life + 100 years ended in 1998, so the text is public domain there from 1 January 1999.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
